newsitem.title: FRANCE: French air strike adds to transport woes.
newsitem.headline: French air strike adds to transport woes.

text.p: A strike by French pilots and crews cut flights on Wednesday, aggravating woes for travellers on the 10th day of a stoppage by truckers choking highways and slowly strangling the French economy.

State-owned Air France said it was guaranteeing two-thirds of long-haul flights and a quarter of medium-distance flights during the two-day strike, over grievances such as deregulation of air transport in Europe and feared job and pay cuts.
Air France Europe, the short-haul unit of Air France, said it was axing more than half its flights during the strike that began on Wednesday.

It said it was sticking to a reduced plan for 213 flights on Wednesday and 200 on Thursday, against 480 normally each day. "There are no delays to the reduced service," said spokeswoman Fabienne de Brebisson.
An Air France cargo official said he expected to cancel six of 14 jumbo freight flights scheduled over the two days.

The strike coincided with the 10th day of a strike by truck drivers seeking higher pay, shorter hours and earlier retirement. Truckers unions vowed to tighten their blockades despite progress in marathon talks overnight with employers.

The USPNT air union said an "overwhelming majority" of pilots and crews were on strike and that Air France had called in planes and crews from Switzerland, Belgium, Turkey, Britain and even the United States to plug gaps.

It accused Air France chairman Christian Blanc of snubbing an invitation by Transport Minister Bernard Pons to meet unions and of failing to protect airlines from the economic and social hardships of deregulation in Europe.
"Blanc...still wants to set French air transport on the road towards a system like that of flags of convenience used by the merchant navy," it said.
Small airline AOM, owned by the state-backed CDR holding company, said nine of its 10 flights left as scheduled on Wednesday morning. The scrapped flight was on the Paris-Marseille route.
Other flights were expected to be unaffected.
Air Liberte said that its flights, about 30-40 a day, had been untouched by the strikes.
